subject: Economics
title: Exchange rate management and buffer stocks

stages.name: Emerging and developing economies: exchange rate management and buffer stocks
stages.title: Exchange rate management and buffer stocks
stages.sub: After this stage you can explain why developing economies might manage their exchange rate rather than let it float, and how a buffer stock scheme stabilises volatile commodity prices.

steps.q: A developing country lets its currency float freely. A sudden drop in demand for its main export causes the currency to lose 30% of its value in a month, making imported food and fuel much more expensive overnight. Is this swing something the country can control?
steps.right: No, the value moves wherever the market takes it
steps.wrong: Yes, the government can stop it happening
steps.hint: Under a market-set system, who decides the value day to day?

steps.q: After seeing how damaging that swing was, the government decides to step in and keep the currency trading within a set band against the dollar, buying or selling currency whenever it drifts outside. What kind of system is this?
steps.right: One where the government actively controls the exchange rate
steps.wrong: One where the market sets the exchange rate freely
steps.hint: Is the value now left to supply and demand alone, or is someone steering it?

steps.q: With the currency now held steady in its band, importers and exporters can sign contracts months ahead without worrying the exchange rate will suddenly wreck their costs. Does this steadiness help firms plan investment?
steps.wrong: No, firms still cannot plan easier
steps.hint: Think about what a stable, predictable rate does for anyone signing a long-term deal.

steps.q: To hold the currency in its band, the central bank must constantly buy or sell foreign currency using its reserves, and those reserves are limited. If a huge wave of selling hits the currency, can the bank defend the band forever?
steps.right: No, it can run out of reserves eventually
steps.wrong: Yes, it can defend the band forever
steps.hint: The bank is using up a limited stock of foreign currency each time it intervenes.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: A cocoa-farming country sees world cocoa prices swing wildly year to year, wrecking farmers' incomes. The government sets a floor price below which it will buy up unsold cocoa, and a ceiling price above which it will sell cocoa from its stores. Is this a floor alone, or a full price band?
steps.right: A full band, with both a floor and a ceiling
steps.wrong: A floor alone, with no ceiling
steps.hint: The government reacts both when price falls too low and when it rises too high.
